note: Runs produced by `make bench` and nothing else. Every entry carries the protocol that produced it, because a throughput number without one cannot be compared to anything -- that is what went wrong with headline_results.json, whose rows record no seq_len and whose Pi 'decode 17.4' turned out to be a short-context figure while the same build reads 12.8 at 512 tokens. The baseline is measured only after the board has returned to the temperature geist started from; without that the ratio measures the running order as much as the engines. Rows are appended by `make bench BENCH_ARGS=--record`; a plain `make bench` never writes here, so a stranger reproducing the numbers leaves no diff behind. Throughput is hardware-bound and therefore context, not comparison; the ratio column is the part that carries across machines.

schema.system: CPU as the machine names itself
schema.cores: logical cores visible to the process
schema.commit: geist commit the binary was built from
schema.protocol: frozen sweep parameters -- rows with differing protocols are not comparable
schema.decode_tps_512: decode throughput at a 512-token prompt, mean of the repeats
schema.spread_pct: run-to-run spread as +/-% around the mean. Above ~2% the run varied; read it together with load before blaming contention -- on an idle board it is usually thermal drift over a long sweep
schema.decode_tps_short: decode throughput at the shortest prompt -- the row that matches a baseline's empty-context generation benchmark
schema.j_per_decode_token: board energy per decoded token, from the phase-separated probes
schema.j_per_prefill_token: board energy per prefill token, from the prefill-only probe
schema.baselines: every competing engine measured in the same run, each with its own start temperature and gate status. A list because a box can carry more than one relevant opponent -- bitnet.cpp for ternary, llama.cpp otherwise -- and measuring only the first silently dropped llama.cpp everywhere both existed
